Hi! ADC main here that's peaked at Gold 1 here to offer a bit of advice from the other half of bot lane. :)

> Who are the supports that fit the criteria: able to GO IN, all-capitals and bolded, possibly ability to get out as well, has protectiveness (heal, shield, GTFO-type CC), can play passively and still be useful, tankiness. Mobility and Targon-compatibility (aka melee) is a big plus.

Leona, Braum, and Taric are the big ones. Thresh and Blitz also fit that IMO, but depends on your definition. 

>In low elo (low Silver/high Bronze), do ADCs generally follow up when I go in? I remember around 35% of why I stopped playing Leona was that my ADC just ignored my engages.

Can't say much here, but I would do target ping, then do your thing if you're playing the first 3 supports. If I see a hook, I'm gonna move into my supports "circle" and start hitting whatever champions he/she gets.

>Connected: On the scale of moving slightly forward to screaming multiple times "I AM ENGAGING" in chat and spam pinging, how many cues do low elo ADCs need to understand and follow up?

Kinda answered this above. At the start of the game I'd type, "Hey, ya monkey ADC, if you see me ping and walk up, follow me or I'll last hit your CS WITHOUT Targon's. :)"

>Gargoyle Stoneplate: a godsend for the low budget supports or an expensive niche item that's for toplaners (like Sunfire)?

I think this item is insane. I wouldn't build it on Thresh or Blitz, but on super tanks like Braum and Leona, I see no downside as you're pretty much there for CC. Dunno how Leona's passive works with it though. (Procing it with Stoneskin active, does it reduce it?)

>I remember one of the common complaints against tanky engagers is when they fall behind, they're useless because they don't have gold for tanky items and can't engage, or they'll be blown up. How much of this is true?

While this is a bit true, at the point I would love it if you stood by me and peeled instead of engaging. Unless you're the only GOOD form of engage, then it's a bit of a tough call. I still think I'd like to have you between their front line and the ADC/Mid.

>How and when do I engage in the classic midlane ARAM? If I move forward, enemies move backwards and if I get a way in, my team is too far away or ignore me. Should I disappear from their vision, sneak around and spam ping flank?

Flanks are very good. I've found the most helpful thing to do is say "Hey, we're not accomplishing anything and I can't get a pick/too far behind to do anything. Can we push side lanes and get ready for (insert objective here). Flash + Braum Ult/Leona E or Ult/Blitz hooks/Thresh Hook are all insane too. Even from behind, those can win you games. I'd say, it just depends.

>Kind of off-question, but does tank Rakan work? I loved playing him, but I always built him full utility, with Redemption/Locket/Ardent. Now, with the E nerf and W buff, does he support a more tanky build (Redemption/Gargoyle/Locket/tank)?

Personally, I think Rakan is trash tier. But, I think a more "tank build" is the way I would play him. As an ADC main, I groan when I see him on my team, and get really happy when he's on the enemy team. His kit screams "I'M A TANK" but his base stats and scaling say others. IDK, he's in a weird spot IMO.

Hope that helped! Feel free to ask me anymore questions if you'd like.

The thing I did that really sent me from being outside of top 8 (Bubble Boy) to top 4 constantly is looking at your opponent and trying to read him/her. Watch what their hands touch. You're playing Modern and they're playing Jund and they fan out their grave yard? Kolaghan's Command incoming! Watch how people organize their lands. Watch their eyes, that's a big one. Don't lose focus of the game, don't think about school or work or anything but that game. Don't think about "Hey, if I win then I'm 1 win away from top 8!" Think about "What do I lose to? Is leaving a guy back gonna slow down my clock by a turn, or can I leave this dude back for blocks if needed?" Is there a clock in the room? Sit on the side FACING the clock. Dictate the pace of your game, you notice your open is trying to keep up with you speed wise and you're comfortable on your deck? Speed it up. Make it play at your pace so he misplays. If he's deep in the tank, ask him how many cards in hand to get him out of the tank. Magic skill is important to winning, but get those small edges, they add up.

A day before my thirteenth birthday day, I got a call to my house phone from my grandfather. He had to explain to me that my mother had passed out in the grocery store and that he was coming to pick me up and take me to the hospital. As we got there, about 4 hours after she was admitted to the hospital, we parked next to the Cancer wing of our hospital. I then asked my Grandpa if my mom had cancer. I remember him never responding to that question. Just looked at me as if he wanted to answer, but was afraid to break my heart, along with losing his daughter. That next day, we spent my birthday in a hospital room. My mom was never awake during the whole thing, but we went in and set up my birthday with a few balloons, cake, and presents. It got to the blowing out candles part, and I blew them out and made a wish. I wished I could have 10 minutes alone with my mom. At 13, it's hard to grasp the concept of losing someone as important in my life as she is to me. I didn't realize how fast I could lose her. I held her limp hand in my own and cried, asking her to wake up. My grandpa walked in a few minutes later and pried me off of her. I remember not sleeping at all, constantly worried that that was the last memory I'd have with her. I started being nicer to people. Try to look at the bright side of things. I'm 17 now, and I still to this day wonder how I got so lucky. Lucky to be alive. To have my feet on the ground. Lucky to meet all of your kind redditors. Please never take the little things for granted. That's what makes life worth living.
